source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide why the same table measured in handspans can give different numbers for different students.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Different handspan sizes must give different counts, whatever the lengths of the tables.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: The student with the larger handspan will count more handspans.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Their centimetre measurements differ because a centimetre is a different length for each student.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The taller student will count fewer handspans, even if their handspans are the same size.

intelligence.enrichment: A measurement number depends on the length of the unit used. Body-part units such as handspan, hand, foot, fist, or fingers differ from person to person, so the same length can be expressed by different counts. different body-part unit lengths -> different counts for the same object length The learner correctly applies this rule: A measurement number depends on the length of the unit used. Body-part units such as handspan, hand, foot, fist, or fingers differ from person to person, so the same length can be expressed by different counts. A bigger measurement number means the object itself is longer, even when different handspans were used.
